optimizedDescription.value: Central Change entity owns named spec-work lifecycle, approvals, artifacts, invalidation, implementation tracking, and immutable history.

optimizedContext.value:
# Change

## Rules

- Identity: immutable unique slug `name`, immutable `createdAt`; reject whole-slug Windows device names case-insensitively on every OS: `con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com1`–`com9`, `lpt1`–`lpt9`. Larger valid slugs such as `con-foo` remain legal. Every event requires `ActorIdentity`: `name`, `email`, optional `provider`, `providerId`, `metadata: Record<string, string>`.
- Revision: persist `updatedAt`; default to `createdAt`; never before `createdAt`. `touchUpdatedAt(at: Date = new Date())` sets or advances it.
- Scope: mutable, possibly empty `specIds`. Creation validates workspace component against `specd.yaml`, not filesystem spec path. Any `specIds` change invalidates approvals. `workspaces` is non-persisted runtime getter via `parseSpecId()`; plural touched set only, empty for empty `specIds`; no home/primary workspace. Template variables and archive paths MUST NOT derive singular workspace from `workspaces[0]` or another index.
- `specDependsOn`: optional per-spec map; highest-priority `CompileContext` `dependsOn` source; updates do not append `invalidated`. `updateSpecIds()` removes entries whose keys leave `specIds`. Other dependencies resolve dynamically and transitively from each spec `.specd-metadata.yaml` on every `CompileContext` run.
- Lifecycle: `drafting → designing → ready → implementing ⇄ verifying → done → archivable → archiving`. Optional `approvals.spec` inserts `pending-spec-approval → spec-approved` between `ready` and `implementing`; optional `approvals.signoff` inserts `pending-signoff → signed-off` between `done` and `archivable`. Both default `false`; disabled gate states are unreachable. Archive only from `archivable`; otherwise throw `InvalidStateTransitionError`.
- From `archiving`, only `archivable` and `designing` are valid. Pre-commit failures remain `archivable`. Commit failure attempts batch canonical restore: success transitions `archiving → archivable`; restore failure remains `archiving` pending manual `designing`. Successful archive move is not rolled back by metadata generation or post-hook failure; success traceability belongs to archived record.
- Every state except `drafting` MAY return to `designing`. `designing → designing` is state-preserving: no approval invalidation or artifact downgrade. Returning from later state requires artifact review but does not imply drift.
- `implementing → verifying` may repeat and is gated by workflow `taskCompletionCheck` through `verifying.requires`; this checks artifact content, not approval. `implementation-failure` returns to `implementing`, preserves unchanged artifacts/approvals, and resets only artifacts in `implementing.requires`. `artifact-review-required` returns to `designing`. Any `drifted-pending-review` file invalidates to `designing`.
- Implementation tracking is separate from artifacts. `trackedImplementationFiles` use project-relative paths and state `open|resolved|ignored|removed`. `removed` remains historical, is not implicit untrack, cannot reopen through `resolve`, and returns to `open` only when refresh confirms existence. `implementationLinks` support file links `spec -> file` and symbol refinements `spec -> file -> symbols`; active paths remain project-relative, normalized to `workspace:path` at archive materialization.
- Preserve explicit file-level links versus container-only symbol sets: removing last symbol MAY remove container-only set; MUST preserve explicitly created file link.
- `implementationTrackingStartedAt: Date | null`; `isImplementationTrackingActive` iff non-null. `startImplementationTracking(at?: Date)` records once and preserves original timestamp. Historical implementation signal scans history for any `transitioned` event with `to: implementing`; entity performs no file detection. Once true, draft/discard fail unless force override.
- Artifacts: schema-typed `ChangeArtifact` has `type`, `optional`, ordered `requires`, persisted aggregate `state`, `files: Map<string, ArtifactFile>`. `scope: change` typically one type-keyed file; `scope: spec` one file per `specIds`. `ArtifactFile` has `key`, `filename`, explicit persisted `state`, `validatedHash`, `hasDrift`. Hash applies schema `preHashCleanup`; `"__skipped__"` is optional-skip sentinel.
- Canonical states: `missing|in-progress|complete|skipped|pending-review|drifted-pending-review`. Explicit state plus current presence is authoritative; `validatedHash` is baseline only. Aggregate priority: any `drifted-pending-review`; else any `pending-review`; else all `complete`/`skipped` with files => `complete`; all `skipped` with files => `skipped`; all `missing` or no files => `missing`; otherwise `in-progress`.
- Effective `pending-parent-artifact-review`: recursively blocked while upstream artifact-DAG parent is `drifted-pending-review` or `pending-review`; aggregate applies when no file has those direct states and at least one has `pending-parent-artifact-review`. `LifecycleEngine` owns recursive interpretation.
- Only `optional: true` artifacts may be `skipped`; actor sets skip explicitly. Only `complete` and `skipped` satisfy `requires`. `ChangeArtifact.markComplete(key, hash)` is exclusive to `ValidateArtifacts`; sets file `complete`, updates `validatedHash`, recomputes aggregate. `markSkipped()` marks ALL files and is exclusive to skip use case.
- Return to `designing`, including scope change while already there, makes previously validated files require review; existing `drifted-pending-review` remains. Exact reopening is governed by invalidation policy.
- `syncArtifacts(artifactTypes)` reconciles schema types and expected scope/`specIds` files, removes obsolete types/files, returns changed flag, and on change appends `artifacts-synced` with additions/removals and `SYSTEM_ACTOR` `{ name: "specd", email: "system@getspecd.dev", provider: "system" }`.
- History is append-only and lifecycle-authoritative. State is latest `transitioned.to`, else `drafting`; no state snapshot. Drafted iff latest `drafted|restored` is `drafted`. Active approval is latest `spec-approved` or `signed-off` without later `invalidated`. Common event fields: `type`, ISO `at`, mandatory `by`.
- Events: `created` (`specIds`, `schemaName`, `schemaVersion`); `transitioned`; `spec-approved`/`signed-off` (`reason`, `artifactHashes`); `invalidated` (`cause`, `message`, `affectedArtifacts`); `drafted`; `restored`; `artifact-skipped`; `artifacts-synced`; `description-updated`; `discarded`; `archive-failed` (`step: prepare|commit|archive`, `message`, `commitStarted`). `archive-failed` records failed active attempt, not archive completion.
- `invalidated.cause`: `spec-change|artifact-drift|artifact-review-required|spec-overlap-conflict`. `affectedArtifacts` entries are `{ type, files }`, with artifact key for `scope: change` and spec ID for `scope: spec`; deduplicate. One drift pass records all drifted files in one event. `spec-overlap-conflict` names archived change and overlapping spec IDs, then appends transition to `designing`.
- `created` captures active `schemaName`/`schemaVersion`; top-level hydrated properties are definitive. Name mismatch throws `SchemaMismatchError` before work. Same-name version mismatch warns but remains usable and archivable.
- Draft moves `changes/` to `drafts/`, appending `drafted` without lifecycle change. Restore moves back, appends `restored`, and only `RestoreChange` via `ChangeRepository.mutateDraft` may perform it. Discard moves active/draft to `discarded/`, appends irreversible `discarded` with mandatory `reason`/`by`, optional `supersededBy`. Historical implementation requires force for draft/discard.
- Drafted changes are read-only. Forbidden: lifecycle transitions, persisted validation, scope edits, approvals, invalidations, implementation-tracking updates, transforming artifact writes. Only restore/discard via `mutateDraft` may transform. Inspect through `ChangeRepository.getDraft` or `GetDraft`, returning `DraftedChangeView`. Active-only lookup throws `ChangeNotFoundError`; invalid low-level mutation throws `DraftedChangeReadOnlyError`.
- `Change.invalidate()` requires cause, message, focused `affectedArtifacts`, `artifactDag: ArtifactDag`, optional `invalidationPolicyOverride`. Effective policy: override else persisted `invalidationPolicy`. Always append `invalidated`; transition to `designing` when prior state differs. `none`: reopen none solely from invalidation; `surgical`: normalized targets; `downstream`: targets plus `artifactDag.descendantsOf()`; `global`: all files. Deduplicate. Never derive DAG edges from persisted `requires` or private BFS.
- `hasDrift` persists independently of canonical state and baseline. Set true only for `artifact-drift` and focused files; changed content or absence counts. `artifact-review-required` neither sets nor clears it. Human views MAY render `complete` plus drift as `complete-with-drift`; canonical `missing` remains `missing`.
- `Change` owns persisted facts: history, state, artifacts/files, aggregate states, approvals, invalidations. `LifecycleEngine` alone interprets schema DAG, workflow `requires`, recursive parent blocking, approval routing, reachability, effective artifact status, next blocker.

## Constraints

- `name`, `createdAt` immutable; `updatedAt >= createdAt`; reserved whole-slug Windows device names rejected universally.
- Empty `specIds` valid; `workspaces` derived, plural, non-persisted; never a primary workspace.
- History immutable; lifecycle derived from history only.
- File state explicit; `validatedHash` baseline only; `hasDrift` independent; reopening policy-driven.
- `skipped` optional-only and satisfies `requires`; completion/skip mutations restricted to designated use cases.
- Both approval gates opt-in and default false; archive only from `archivable`.
- `verifying → implementing` preserves approvals and resets only `implementing.requires`.
- `designing → designing` preserves approvals and artifact states.
- Draft/discard after historical `implementing` requires force; discard irreversible.
- Schema-aware effective status, blockers, routing, and step availability belong only to `LifecycleEngine`.
